evidence.excerpt: Big arena tour, tickets went live at 10am on a Friday, and payments started failing about four minutes in.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Jordan
evidence.note: The trigger event was a payment failure during an arena on-sale.

evidence.excerpt: Their provider's support was a ticket form. They got a reply after the on-sale was over.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Jordan
evidence.note: Incumbent support failed in the moment, which shaped what the customer valued.

evidence.excerpt: The CEO was getting screenshots on social.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Jordan
evidence.note: CEO visibility turned the failure into an executive priority.

evidence.excerpt: So Monday morning the COO, Halima, says they're replacing payments before the spring on-sales.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Jordan
evidence.note: Halima set the deadline and scope: replace payments before spring.

evidence.excerpt: Ben, their CTO, said twice. But this was the first time the CEO saw it.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Ben
evidence.note: Earlier failures did not trigger a search; CEO visibility did.

evidence.excerpt: Halima. Ben wanted us.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Jordan
evidence.note: Decider was Halima; the technical champion preferred us.

evidence.excerpt: He told me that, and he told me he lost.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Ben
evidence.note: Ben told the rep he lost the internal decision.

evidence.excerpt: it was Halima's call and she made it in one meeting.
evidence.label: quote
evidence.speaker: Ben
evidence.note: Customer's own words that the decision was Halima's and was made quickly.

evidence.excerpt: They showed up with the people who'd actually be on the account. A named solutions engineer and an account lead, in the room.
evidence.label: fact
evidence.speaker: Ben
evidence.note: The competitor brought named people to the meeting, per Ben.

evidence.excerpt: there'd be a shared channel and someone on call for every major on-sale

evidence.label: fact

evidence.note: The customer's questions shifted from technical topics to people after the competitor meeting.

contradictions.what: The rep says we were the favourite, but Halima, not Ben, decided and chose the competitor. Ben's preference was not the deciding vote.
The rep thought the load test had won it, but Halima's only reaction to it was 'good.' and she moved on.
The rep walked through support plans, but the customer never used the word support and asked for a person.
The rep calls us the better platform, yet the customer chose the competitor, and Halima said she does not buy uptime.
The rep says we were the favourite right before Halima's sentence, but also reports the earlier silence when she asked who her person was.

dodges.question: What did the customer bring up about the competitor?
dodges.what: The competitor is never named. The rep relays Ben's report, then adds an unverified guess about over-promising and admits 'I don't know that'.

outcome_signals.what: Lost. Ben told the rep he lost and the decision went to the competitor.
The customer was replacing payments entirely, so the whole payments business was in play. No partial split is mentioned.
Halima decided in one meeting, after the competitor meeting shifted the questions to named support.
